title: West Asia war, the Strait of Hormuz and India’s oil bill
dek: How the US–Iran conflict disrupted the world’s most important oil route, and why it matters so much to India.
seoTitle: Strait of Hormuz crisis 2026: oil and India
bigLabel: Down about 20% from a late-October peak near $118

glance.what: Since the war began, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted. Brent peaked near $118 in late October, then fell sharply in November as Qatar mediated talks between Iran and the US, before rebounding on fresh attacks.
glance.why: India imports most of its crude oil, and a large share of its oil, LNG and almost all its LPG has passed through Hormuz. The government says it absorbed ₹43 of a needed ₹50-a-litre diesel increase.
glance.next: Whether the Qatar-brokered proposal to reopen Hormuz goes anywhere. On 12 November President Trump said the US did not need a deal with Iran.

forYou: Higher oil prices feed into petrol, diesel, cooking gas and airfares, and weaken the rupee.
next: Whether Hormuz reopens under the Qatar-brokered proposal.

events.title: Strikes on Iran; the Strait of Hormuz closes
events.summary: After US and Israeli strikes on Iran, Hormuz shipping is shut. Brent ends the week near a seven-month high of about $73.

events.title: Tankers hit; shipping lines suspend Hormuz routes
events.summary: At least three tankers are damaged and Maersk suspends all cargo through the strait. Brent closed above $79 on 3 March, up from about $65 before the crisis.

events.title: Brent crosses $100
events.summary: Oil climbs back above $100 a barrel as the disruption drags on.

events.title: Blockade continues as peace talks stall
events.summary: Brent trades at $102.40 on 23 April and above $106 the next day.

events.title: Ceasefire news brings relief
events.summary: Brent falls about 4% to around $84 on news of a ceasefire and hopes that Hormuz shipping will normalise.

events.title: Oil back above $90
events.summary: A US–Iran deadlock keeps Hormuz disrupted, raising India’s import bill and pressure on the rupee.

events.title: Brent nears $100 again
events.summary: A fresh escalation in the US–Iran conflict renews fears for Gulf supplies, with Hormuz shipping still severely disrupted.

events.title: Saudi pipeline hit; Brent above $107
events.summary: An Iranian ship is attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline, used to bypass the strait, is damaged in a drone attack. Brent crosses $107 even as the US says it is escorting more tankers.

events.title: Oil peaks near $118
events.summary: Brent climbs to a late-October peak of about $118 a barrel after tankers are struck in the strait, its highest close in six months.

events.title: Qatar talks: oil plunges about 8%
events.summary: After weekend mediation talks between Iran and Qatar, a draft proposal to end the war circulates, reportedly centred on reopening Hormuz. Brent settles 7.6% lower, even as tankers near the strait are hit.

events.title: Iran's Hormuz plan goes to the White House
events.summary: Qatar's prime minister takes an Iranian proposal to reopen Hormuz to President Trump. Under the reported plan, the US would lift its blockade and release $8 billion in frozen funds. A Qatari official called one report of the terms false. Brent falls to its lowest close since 31 August.
events.differs: An Israeli outlet reported Iran had dropped its demand to charge tolls in the strait; a Qatari official told Bloomberg that report was false.

events.title: Trump says no deal needed; oil jumps 3%
events.summary: Trump posts that the US does not need a deal with Iran. Houthis claim attacks on Saudi energy sites, and Iran's military reports tankers hit in the strait. Brent settles 3.3% higher at $95.82. In India, PM Modi says the government absorbed ₹43 of a needed ₹50-a-litre diesel increase.
